title: Uncountable pair colourings: positive results and counterexamples
summary: Sierpiński forbids uncountable homogeneous sets; Dushnik–Miller guarantees a large set in one colour or an infinite set in the other.
abstract: If every pair of natural numbers is coloured red or blue, Ramsey's theorem guarantees an infinite set all of whose pairs have one colour. Replacing ‘infinite’ by ‘uncountable’ changes the answer: pairs from the first uncountable ordinal can be coloured so that no uncountable subset has one colour throughout. Yet every two-colouring there has either an uncountable set with all pairs red or a countably infinite set with all pairs blue. Allowing different target sizes for the two colours recovers a positive theorem, which also holds at every regular infinite cardinal.
